solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Helicopter heading off, one making short trip?

indicators.note: the head of the word, its first letter, is taken off

parts.note: the informal name for a helicopter, from the chopping sound of its rotor blades

explanation.surface: A helicopter sets off on a short hop somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' looks like the aircraft departing, but it strips the first letter from the slang word for a helicopter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that hops makes short jumps or brief journeys, as a kangaroo, a flea or an island-hopping traveller does.

clue.text: Orthodox believer possesses half-formed notion

parts.note: to possess something is to have it: he has

indicators.note: only half of the word for a notion is formed, so its second half is dropped

parts.note: a notion is an idea

explanation.surface: A devout person is said to cling to an idea that is not fully worked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-formed' drops EA, the second half of IDEA, leaving ID.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hasid is a member of a strictly Orthodox Jewish movement, so an example of a believer of that kind.

clue.text: Claim poet is misguided, having old-fashioned ideas about the stars?

definitions.text: having old-fashioned ideas about the stars?

indicators.note: something misguided has gone astray, so these letters are led into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a poet's claim as mistaken and out of date in its astronomy.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of CLAIM POET gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ptolemy's ancient system put the Earth at the centre with the stars and planets circling it, a view long since abandoned.

clue.text: Make listener listen finally

parts.note: the ear is the organ that listens

indicators.note: only the final letter of the word listen is taken

explanation.surface: An order to force someone who hears to pay attention at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally' takes N, the last letter of 'listen'.
explanation.definitionFit: To make money is to earn it, as in making a good salary.

clue.text: Piano player ultimately avoids Chopin's pieces maybe

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, meaning softly

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very last letter of player

parts.note: to avoid someone is to elude them

explanation.surface: A pianist ends up skipping some of Chopin's works.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ultimately' takes R, the last letter of 'player'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopin wrote a famous set of twenty-four short piano introductory pieces in every key; the question mark marks them as one example.

clue.text: Precious one getting lost somehow gets back

indicators.note: the letter for one is lost from the word precious before the rest is rearranged
somehow says the remaining letters are put together in some other way

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A treasured object goes missing but is somehow recovered.
explanation.walkthrough: PRECIOUS with I removed leaves PRECOUS, and 'somehow' rearranges those letters into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoup losses is to recover or regain them, getting back what was spent.

clue.text: Hiding pain, the Parisian wastes away

indicators.note: the French article hides the word for pain by wrapping round it

parts.note: les is French for the (plural), as said in Paris
anguish is severe pain or distress

explanation.surface: A Parisian conceals his suffering while wasting away.
explanation.definitionFit: To languish is to grow weak or feeble, pining or fading over time.

clue.text: Crowd departs on journey lacking purpose?

parts.note: d is the abbreviation for departs on timetables
to rove is to wander about with no fixed aim

explanation.surface: A mass of people heads off on an aimless trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crowd' looks like a verb but is the noun for a herd or throng.
explanation.definitionFit: A drove is a herd of animals being driven, and by extension a large moving crowd of people.

clue.text: Team on top of list? One could be up against the wall!

definitions.text: One could be up against the wall!

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: a side is a team in sport
a table is a list such as a league table

explanation.surface: A team tops the league list, and something finds itself under pressure, pinned to the wall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up against the wall' suggests a desperate situation; literally the piece of furniture stands against a wall.
explanation.definitionFit: A side table is a small table placed against a wall or beside something, so it literally stands against it.

clue.text: Charlie departing for good in order to get academic award

indicators.note: one letter departs and another comes in for it

parts.note: a decree is an official order
Charlie is C in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Charlie leaves for good so as to collect a university qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'departing for good' reads like leaving permanently, but C is swapped for G in DECREE.
explanation.definitionFit: A university awards a degree, such as a BA or PhD, on completion of study.

clue.text: Problem with electricity supply has firm in torment

indicators.note: the power spike has the firm held within it

parts.note: a surge is a sudden damaging rise in voltage
co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A power fault leaves a company suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Problem with electricity supply' is a single long definition-like phrase, yet it is only a piece of wordplay; 'torment' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourge is a whip or anything that causes great suffering, a source of torment.

clue.text: Agreement to impose restraining influence on prisoner

indicators.note: in an across entry the restraint placed on the prisoner comes after it

parts.note: con is slang for a convict, a prisoner
a cord is something that ties or binds, restraining

explanation.surface: A pact to keep an inmate under control.
explanation.definitionFit: Concord is harmony or agreement between people or nations, also a formal treaty.

clue.text: Appealed, having switched sides, for subs

indicators.note: having switched says a letter changes its place, here the one at the far end crossing over
the sides are the letters at either end of the word, each moving to the other edge

parts.note: to sue is to appeal or petition, and also to go to court

explanation.surface: Someone appealed after changing allegiance, all for the sake of membership fees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having switched sides' swaps the end letters of SUED, S and D, giving the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Subs is short for subscriptions, the membership fees owed to a club or society.

clue.text: Artful nude, terribly dishonest

indicators.note: terribly suggests something done badly, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A crafty nude picture is shockingly deceitful.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of ARTFUL NUDE gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraud is deception for gain, so something fraudulent is deceitful and untrustworthy.

clue.text: Disruptions — music-maker is not playing

parts.note: a viola is a stringed instrument, a maker of music

indicators.note: the letters are at play, moving about into a new order

explanation.surface: Interruptions arise because an instrument is silent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges IS NOT into TIONS, the opposite of what the surface says.
explanation.definitionFit: Violations of rules or peace are breaches that disrupt order, so the two words overlap in sense.

clue.text: Caution about English — result of much study?

indicators.note: the word for caution goes about, round, the single letter

parts.note: wariness is caution, being on guard

explanation.surface: A warning about English, possibly following long study.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts E inside WARINESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Long hours of study bring tiredness, and the Bible says much study is a weariness of the flesh.

clue.text: Kind of average temperature after spring

indicators.note: the average and temperature come after the spring

parts.note: a well is a source of water, a spring
the mean is the average

explanation.surface: A sort of mean temperature following springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kind' looks like 'sort of' but it is the definition, an adjective; 'spring' is the water source, not the season.
explanation.definitionFit: A kind gesture is well-intentioned, done with good intentions even if clumsy.

clue.text: Plant for making mixed drink

definitions.meaning: a woody bush smaller than a tree
an old cordial of fruit juice, sugar and rum or vinegar

explanation.surface: A plant that is grown to flavour a cocktail.
explanation.definitionFit: A bush is a low woody plant, and the same word names a punch of citrus, sugar and spirits or a vinegar-based cordial.

clue.text: Exposing cleric somewhere in London

parts.note: rev is short for reverend, a cleric
Ealing is a district of west London, famous for its film studios

explanation.surface: Uncovering a clergyman somewhere in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: EALING is a district of west London, once home to the Ealing comedy films.
explanation.definitionFit: Something revealing shows what was hidden, as a revealing dress or remark does.

clue.text: The French officer retreats, becoming confined

indicators.note: an army that retreats goes back, so the letters read backwards

parts.note: la is French for the (feminine)
col is the abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: A French officer withdraws and finds himself hemmed in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreats' turns LACOL backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Something local is restricted to one area, as a local anaesthetic is limited to one part of the body.

clue.text: Fellow works to produce plan

parts.note: a fellow is a man
oeuvre is the body of an artist's works

explanation.surface: A man produces a body of work to create a scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A manoeuvre is a scheme or tactic, a move planned to gain advantage.

clue.text: Place for three men in a boat, reported author

indicators.note: reported means the place name is said aloud, sounding the same as the writer

parts.words: Place for three men in a boat
parts.note: Marlow is the Thames town reached in Jerome K Jerome's comic novel Three Men in a Boat

explanation.surface: The writer named after a Thames town where three men rowed.
explanation.walkthrough: Marlow is a riverside town in Buckinghamshire, England, on the route of the boating trip in Three Men in a Boat.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe was the Elizabethan dramatist who wrote Doctor Faustus and Tamburlaine.

clue.text: No time for stifling expression of disgust, revealing nothing

indicators.note: the two outer pieces stifle the exclamation by enclosing it

parts.note: taken as written
ugh is an exclamation of disgust

explanation.surface: Not having time to suppress a groan of revulsion shows emptiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Nought is the figure zero, meaning nothing at all.

clue.text: Bit of skeleton encountered west of a Turkish city

indicators.note: in an across entry, west of means to the left of, coming before

parts.note: to encounter someone is to meet them; past tense met
Tarsus is a city in southern Turkey, birthplace of St Paul

explanation.surface: Someone meets a contact on the western side of a city in Turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The metatarsus is the group of five long bones in the foot, part of the skeleton.

clue.text: Attempted to get lid off box of delights?

indicators.note: in a down entry the lid is the top letter, which comes off

parts.note: to strive is to attempt hard; past tense of strive

explanation.surface: Someone tried to prise the lid off a treasure chest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get lid off' removes S, the top letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A treasure trove is a hoard of valuables, figuratively a store or box of delightful things.

clue.text: Shopping facility everyone's found by motorway

parts.note: m is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1
everyone is all

explanation.surface: Everybody heads to the shopping centre beside the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'everyone's' is everyone is, giving ALL; a motorway is a British highway, numbered with M.
explanation.definitionFit: A mall is a large enclosed shopping centre.

clue.text: Drink in African camp

definitions.meaning: a South African encampment of wagons drawn up in a circle, usually spelt laager

explanation.surface: A beer drunk in a camp in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The beer is a light bottom-fermented brew; the Afrikaans word for a wagon encampment is also written this way.

clue.text: Destructive fly makes one terrified

definitions.meaning: a small fly whose larvae damage cereal crops
a dialect past participle of fright, meaning scared

explanation.surface: A harmful insect scares someone stiff.
explanation.walkthrough: The scared sense is northern English dialect, made famous by Margaret Thatcher's taunt that an opponent was frit.
explanation.definitionFit: The frit fly is a cereal pest, and in British dialect the same word means frightened.

clue.text: Ace, endlessly gloomy, has nothing lovingly expressed

parts.note: a is the abbreviation for ace in cards

indicators.note: the word loses its end, the final letter

parts.note: morose means gloomy and sullen
o, the shape of zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A top player, always downcast, has nothing to say tenderly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' takes E off MOROSE, leaving MOROS.
explanation.definitionFit: Amoroso is a musical direction meaning to play tenderly, with love.

clue.text: Democrat in running to be US President once

indicators.note: the party letter goes in the middle of the running word

parts.note: haring is running fast like a hare
d is the abbreviation for Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A Democrat in the race hopes to become a former president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts D inside HARING. The irony: Warren Harding was a Republican.
explanation.definitionFit: Warren G Harding was the 29th President of the United States, serving 1921 to 1923.

clue.text: He has batted in cricket match briefly — in struggle for this?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go in the shortened match
briefly cuts the word short by its final letter

parts.note: a test is an international cricket match

indicators.note: batted suggests the letters are knocked about into a new order

explanation.surface: A player bats in a short cricket match, perhaps fighting for a trophy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Ashes is the Test cricket series between England and Australia, so the whole clue hints at the prize itself.
explanation.definitionFit: England and Australia play cricket for a tiny urn of burnt remains, the trophy their Test series is named after.

clue.text: Male leading Queen, an experienced performer

indicators.note: the male piece leads, coming before the queen

parts.note: a stag is a male deer
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A man leads the Queen as a seasoned actor.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is the Queen, from Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: An old stager is a veteran, someone long experienced, originally on the stage.
